newsitem.title: NORWAY: NORDIC SKIING-PROKUROROV UPSETS NORWEGIANS TO WIN 30 KM GOLD.
newsitem.headline: NORDIC SKIING-PROKUROROV UPSETS NORWEGIANS TO WIN 30 KM GOLD.

text.p: Russian veteran Alexei Prokurorov surprised himself and the mighty Norwegians to win his first major title in nine years in Friday's 30 km freestyle cross-country race at the Nordic skiing world championships.
Prokurorov, who had entered five previous world championships but had never won gold, chose the opening race of the 10-day festival in Trondheim to taste triumph at last.
Few would have bet on the 32-year-old Russian, who became Olympic champion over the same distance in 1988 in Calgary, as he had never finished in the top 10 in any World Cup meeting this winter.
"I didn't expect to do so well," said Prokurorov after covering two laps of a bumpy 15 kms circuit in a winning time of one hour six minutes 28 seconds.
The thousands of fans lining the track on a beautiful day were hoping for another win for Norwegian Bjorn Daehlie, the most successful cross-country skier of all time.
Daehlie made the strongest start but after 15 kms, he was already two seconds slower than Prokurorov and had to settle for second place 17 seconds behind the winner.
Young Thomas Alsgaard, who was feeling sick and decided to enter the race only at the last minute, brought some consolation to Norway by taking third place 21 seconds behind Prokurorov.
There was disappointment for reigning world champion Vladimir Smirnov of Kazakhstan, who struggled from the start to finish a poor 42nd.
Daehlie, the last competitor to leave the stadium, soon caught Italian Silvio Fauner, who had started 30 seconds before him.
The Norwegian, appearing to move almost effortlessly as he climbed a steep hill in a pine forest nearly halfway through the course, clocked the fastest intermediate time after seven kilometres.
Finn Mika Myllylae was second four seconds behind with Alsgaard third a further four seconds back.
"Prokurorov was nowhere then," said Daehlie. "I didn't hear about him until the end of the first lap when I learned he was two seconds ahead of me. I was a little bit surprised."
Daehlie then failed to keep up with the pace set by Prokurorov as he lost ground on the Russian in the second lap.
"I felt a bit tired in the last uphill sections but I'm not at all disappointed," said the Norwegian, who won six world titles in his brilliant career.
"At one stage, I thought I could go for gold but a silver medal is fine. There are more races to come."
